info.description:
The CoderHelm API lets your own programs start and follow CoderHelm's work: list and inspect runs, retry or cancel them, create and run plans, read the reviewer's reviews, check token usage, manage the webhook endpoints CoderHelm sends your team's events to, and see how deliveries went.

Every request is authenticated with a team API key sent as a bearer token. Admins create keys in the dashboard under Settings, API keys. A key holds scopes, never more than the admin who made it, and has its own rate limit.

CI jobs upload test reports with a GitHub Actions OIDC token instead of a key, and the webhooks are verified by their signatures.
info.title: CoderHelm API

get.description: How the team's deliveries went over a period, against the period before: webhooks CoderHelm received (GitHub, Jira, alerts), events it relayed, and what it sent (webhook endpoints, Slack, Teams, email). Per hour for `24h`, per day otherwise: volume, success rate, latency percentiles, retries and how many of them went fine, failures by reason in plain words, the event types that failed most, and each webhook endpoint's success rate, latency, failure streak and whether it is turned off. Counts are kept 120 days; each delivery's own record 14.

Sanity posts to the address shown for each Sanity source (CoderHelm registers it itself when the token may manage webhooks), signed with `sanity-webhook-signature`: `t=<ms>,v1=` and the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<body>`, keyed with the token in the address; a signature older than five minutes is refused. post.description: On a hybrid self-hosted install, where CoderHelm's hosted relay forwards the events of CoderHelm's GitHub App (and Jira app) after checking the provider's own signature. Each request is signed with the install's relay key: `X-CoderHelm-Relay-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,d=<delivery id>,v1=<hex>,v2=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<d>.<raw body>` and `v2` of `v2.<t>.<d>.<source>.<event>.<raw body>` (so the two headers below are signed too). Both must match: a request without `v2` is refused. Requests older than 5 minutes are refused, and so is a delivery id the install has already taken (`409`). `X-CoderHelm-Relay-Source` is `github` or `jira`; for GitHub, `X-CoderHelm-Relay-Event` is GitHub's event type and the body is GitHub's payload, unchanged.
